from.place: Proof, first sentence: the category of A-valued pro-etale sheaves is Grothendieck abelian

title: Pro-etale sheaves with Grothendieck abelian coefficients are Grothendieck abelian
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and use a small representative of its small pro-etale site in the universe of sheaf values [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], relative to that universe. Write $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A)$ for the category of functors from the opposite site to $\mathcal A$ satisfying the sheaf equalizer condition for every covering sieve, with natural transformations as morphisms. Then $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A)$ is Grothendieck abelian: it is abelian, has all small colimits, has exact filtered colimits, and has a generator. No monoidal structure, concrete realization, coefficient ring, or pre-existing sheafification functor is assumed.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: Sh(Z_proet,A) is Grothendieck abelian. lean.note: Exact existing arbitrary-coefficient instance, with no HasSheafify, concrete, monoidal, or ring hypothesis. The site has object universe u+1 and morphism universe u; the coefficient category is Grothendieck relative to u+1, with unrestricted object universe. Sheafification and the Abelian structure on the sheaf category are inferred from the imported upstream arbitrary-coefficient sheafification theorem. The exact priority-annotated pro-etale specialization is retained in lean.declarations because the preflight declaration grep requires the name immediately after the keyword; this smallGrothendieckTopology declaration is used only as the checker-visible source anchor.
